results.title: CVE-2025-23275 - CVE-2025-23275: Nvidia Cuda Toolkit DOS Vulnerability
results.content:
## Technical Details for CVE-2025-23275

### Vulnerability Analysis

The nvJPEG library provides GPU-accelerated JPEG decoding as part of the NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit. The vulnerability occurs when the library processes image dimensions that fall outside expected boundary conditions. When a local authenticated user submits an image with certain crafted dimensions, nvJPEG writes beyond the intended GPU memory allocation. This out-of-bounds write corrupts adjacent memory regions on the device. Because GPU memory can hold sensitive data from concurrent contexts, corruption can cascade into denial of service and leak residual information from GPU buffers. The attack is constrained to local execution but does not require elevated privileges beyond a standard authenticated session.

### Root Cause [...] ### Attack Vector

Exploitation requires local access with authenticated user privileges. The attacker submits a malformed JPEG or invokes the nvJPEG API with attacker-controlled dimension arguments. No user interaction is needed, and the scope remains unchanged. The result is corruption of GPU memory that can crash CUDA workloads or expose data from other GPU allocations. Refer to the NVIDIA Security Bulletin for technical details specific to the affected components.

## Detection Methods for CVE-2025-23275

### Indicators of Compromise [...] ### Root Cause

The root cause is insufficient validation of image dimension parameters prior to GPU buffer indexing inside nvJPEG. The library trusts caller-provided dimensions when computing write offsets in device memory. Missing bounds checks allow indices to exceed allocated buffer sizes, matching the classic CWE-787 pattern.

results.title: NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit < 13.0 Multiple Vulnerabilities<!-- --> | Tenable®
results.content:
The version of NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit installed on the remote host is prior to 13.0. It is, therefore, affected by multiple vulnerabilities, including the following:  
  
 - NVIDIA nvJPEG contains a vulnerability in jpeg encoding where a user may cause an out-of-bounds read by providing a maliciously crafted input image with dimensions that cause integer overflows in array index calculations. A successful exploit of this vulnerability may lead to denial of service. (CVE-2025-23274)  
  
 - NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit for all platforms contains a vulnerability in nvJPEG where a local authenticated user may cause a GPU out-of-bounds write by providing certain image dimensions. A successful exploit of this vulnerability may lead to denial of service and information disclosure. (CVE-2025-23275)
